doc.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: The decline of jazz parties
summary: Miles discusses jazz parties such as Gibson's and Santa Fe that have ended, and the value of those that continue.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Just a word about this phenomenon of these jazz festivals, these jazz parties, it’s like a great thing for musicians.

It is a great thing. This one’s been going on here in Scottsdale for sixteen or eighteen years. Some of them have dropped by the wayside unfortunately. There were so many of them just a few years ago, let’s say about five, ten years ago there were so many jazz parties all around the country, that a lot of people who wanted to go and hear this one, then wanted to go and hear that one, then wanted to go and hear that one, they couldn’t afford it or some of the parties would overlap and the producers, the promoters wouldn’t work with the other producers and promoters to see if we could all come to some sort of nice agreement as to when you’re going to have yours: “well, last year I had it at this time, I’m not going to change it just because so-and-so’s having one at the same time.” And a few have passed away. Gibson’s jazz party, he’s the granddaddy of jazz parties, he invented the jazz party. That one is rumored to maybe starting back up again you never know. Dick started the whole thing I think it was in Aspen, and then moved it on down to Colorado Springs, and in later years up to Denver. And that hasn’t been happening for a few years. Then there was the Santa Fe party which ran for about five years. That’s gone.

And then there’s a couple of other parties around the country that have hung on for 10 or 15 years and struggled as hard as they could and have done well but then finally just said no, we just can’t do any more, we have to cancel, you know for whatever reason. But thank God there’s still a number of these wonderful parties around the country that we get a chance to play at. And I get a chance to I think maybe if you ask some of the other guys they’ll tell you the same thing, we get a chance to see each other every once in a while. You know sometimes you may not see some of these guys for two or three or five years, and then you have a chance for a couple of days to get back together and play and enjoy your company and tell lies, and all kinds of stuff like that. So it’s a lot of fun though.
